display.title: Episode 186: The Dike and the Shabbos Candles (Tisha B'Av)
display.summary_short: Before Tisha B'Av: Torah, Avodah and Gemilus Chasadim as a diet for the soul, the story of a lost girl brought home by Shabbos candles, and the ancient melody of Eicha.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the Nine Days before Tisha B'Av 5745. Uncle Yossi teaches that the world stands on three things: Torah, our lifeline; Avodah, davening to Hashem, who alone can grant every need, as the Rambam taught; and Gemilus Chasadim, above all daily tzedakah, which also refines our character. This is Hashem's 'diet' for a healthy neshamah over the summer vacation. After an air-conditioner commercial, a first-grade boy recites the Shema. Story time takes place in a Dutch town by the sea. Sisters Leah and Gittel are devoted to each other. When the dike breaks, everyone flees, but Gittel's old injury makes her fall behind. A hard-hearted old woman carries her to her cottage, tells her she has no family left, and works her day and night for three years until Gittel forgets that she is Jewish. Sent to sell butter at a distant fair, Gittel walks home after dark and sees Shabbos candles glowing in a window, and the memories come flooding back. The show ends with a talk on the power of music and the ancient melody of Eicha, the song of golus and hope, and a prayer that Tisha B'Av become a Yom Tov.
display.lesson: Torah, prayer and kindness keep the soul healthy, and the light of a mitzvah like Shabbos candles can bring a lost Jew home.

date.note: No music 'for the past three weeks', Eicha for Tisha B'Av (catalog: 'Eicha, 10 Av', the postponed fast of 5745). Same recording as episode 136 (Tisha B'Av 5744).

advisories.note: A dike breaks and a town flees the flood; a girl is left behind asleep.
A cruel old woman keeps a young girl for three years, works her hard and threatens beatings.
A child is separated from her family and forgets her Jewish life; happy reunion at the end.
Tisha B'Av, golus and the destroyed Beis HaMikdash.
